accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA GCSE Physics 8463 spec 4.2.5.2 (field around a charged object, field pattern for an isolated charged sphere, force on a second charge, field strongest close to the object, sparking explained by the field) and the convention that field direction is the force on a small positive test charge. The ring readouts 36, 9, 4 follow Coulomb's inverse-square law (F proportional to 1/r²) and are labelled as an extension beyond GCSE in the adult text. The sparking description (a strong field ionises air so it conducts; about 3 MV/m in dry air) matches standard texts; the lab's meter is a qualitative model (more charge or smaller gap gives a stronger field) and is not presented as a formula. Parameterised answers k, 2n, 9k and k are whole numbers at every corner because prompts are built as 4k and 9k.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips named in the adult text: lines drawn outwards from a negative charge (flip scene, predict 2, m1, challenge 'sign'), field the same strength everywhere (ring readouts, predict 3, p3, m9, challenge 'same'/'bigger'), no field between drawn lines (m4, challenge 'gap'), lines that cross or circle a single charge (sandbox traces, m2, challenge 'cross'/'cancel'/'circle'), a bigger gap making sparks easier (spark scene, predict 4, m6, challenge 'far'/'less'), contact needed for a force (m8, challenge 'moving') and the force on a negative test charge (p5, challenge 'test'/'none').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagefield is built on field mechanics: a draggable positive test charge whose force arrow is computed from the sphere's sign and inverse-square distance, probes that reveal the radial line through each point, a sign flip that reverses every arrow, rings at 1, 2 and 3 units that record 36, 9 and 4, a spark-gap model with charge and gap controls and a breakdown threshold, and a sandbox that numerically traces field lines from up to four charges. flagstatic (1004) is about charging by friction, attract/repel and conductors; flagqit (1030) is current as charge flow. Lab shingle similarity is under 30% against every other flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: Students find each idea by doing: each probe draws the line in the direction the test charge is pushed, so the outward pattern emerges before the done text names it; flipping the sphere reverses the arrow and the new lines point inwards; dropping on rings shows the arrow shrink and the readout fall 36, 9, 4 as the lines spread; the spark only jumps once charge is high and the gap small, with the meter crossing 'air breaks down'; the sandbox shows lines leaving plus, ending on minus and never crossing.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: 'Inwards, towards it' (probes push the test charge outwards), 'Still pushed away' after the sphere turns negative (the arrow flips to point in), 'The same everywhere in the field' (rings read 36, 9, 4) and 'A bigger gap' (moving the ball away lowers the meter; only closer or more charge sparks).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with ten wrong options; each slip gets its own message: sign (lines show the force on a positive charge, so inwards for negative), circle (radial spokes, circles are the magnetic field round a wire), same/bigger (strongest close, a quarter at twice the distance), gap (lines are a sample), moving (a charge at rest still feels the force), cross/cancel (one direction at each point), far/less (more charge or a smaller gap), test and none (negative charges are pushed against the lines).

readability.evidence: Learner text uses short sentences and defines each term in place (field, field line, test charge, conducts); it passes the learner readability limit in validate_lessons, and the adult text uses the spec wording (isolated charged sphere, test charge, inverse square) within the adult limit. Lab instructions are one or two short sentences per step.

no_filler.evidence: Each learner paragraph carries one idea (what a field is, direction convention, strength and spacing, sparking); adult paragraphs give spec placement, the strength rule and its extension status, named mistakes, and the lab outline. No content-gate filler phrases; feedback lines are all physics.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360x640 screenshots in light and dark: the sphere, rings 1 to 3 and the readout pill fit with labels clear of the rings, the force arrow is visible at every ring, the spark meter now sits under the banner clear of the dome stand and earth post, the sandbox traces fill the stage without clipping the charges, and the full-size button twins wrap two per row. walk.cjs passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a labelled button twin (Probe above/left/below right/right, Make the sphere negative/positive, Test charge on ring 1/2/3, Add/Remove charge, Move ball closer/away, Add + / − charge, Flip the last charge, Reset). The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each force reading and outcome, plus and minus are shown as symbols as well as red and blue, the challenge feedback is a live status region, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found nothing in light or dark on desktop or phone.
